# Url

URLs: parsing, normalizing and resolving them, and reading and building their queries.

## Installation

Add `Url` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Url = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Url` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Allocator`](/docs/api/allocator) 0.1.0
- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`Memory`](/docs/api/memory) 0.1.0
- [`Text`](/docs/api/text) 0.1.0

## Guide

### What it provides

| Module                             | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Url`](/docs/api/url/url#url)     | [`Url`](/docs/api/url/url#url) with [`Parse`](/docs/api/url/url#parse), [`Resolve`](/docs/api/url/url#resolve), component accessors, [`SetPath`](/docs/api/url/url#set-path), [`SetQuery`](/docs/api/url/url#set-query) and [`SetFragment`](/docs/api/url/url#set-fragment), and `HostKind` |
| [`Query`](/docs/api/url/url#query) | [`Pairs`](/docs/api/url/query#pairs) for walking a query's [`QueryPair`](/docs/api/url/query#query-pair)s, [`Decode`](/docs/api/url/query#decode) for turning a component into text, and [`QueryBuilder`](/docs/api/url/query#query-builder)                                                |
| `Error`                            | [`UrlError`](/docs/api/url/error#url-error), why text is not a URL                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import Allocator::SystemAllocator;
import Url::{ Pairs, Url, UrlError };

func SearchTerm(link: char8[..]) -> bool ! UrlError {
    let page = Url::Parse(SystemAllocator(), "https://example.com/docs/index.html")?;
    let target = page.Resolve(link)?;
    for pair in Pairs(target.Query() ?? "") {
        if pair.name.length == 1 && pair.name[0] == 'q' { return true; }
    }
    return false;
}
```

### Design

A URL is read by RFC 3986 and kept as one normalized ASCII text with the place of each component in it, so every accessor is a view and two URLs the RFC calls equivalent under syntax-based normalization are equal as text. Normalizing lower-cases the scheme and a registered host name, writes percent-encoding with upper-case hexadecimal and decodes the escapes of unreserved characters, removes dot segments from the path, leaves out a scheme's default port, and gives an `http`-like URL with an empty path the path `/`. An IPv4 host keeps its dotted form and an IPv6 host is written in the canonical form of RFC 5952. A character a component cannot hold as itself, such as a space or a non-ASCII byte, is percent-encoded rather than refused, as browsers do; a host is the exception, and refuses one, since escaping it would name a different machine. Internationalized host names are not converted to their ASCII form, so a non-ASCII host is refused.

[`Resolve`](/docs/api/url/url#resolve) follows section 5 of RFC 3986, and gives the results of its examples, except that a resolved `http` URL with an empty path is written with `/`. Components stay percent-encoded; [`Decode`](/docs/api/url/query#decode) turns one into text, reading `+` as a space when asked to, as a query is read. [`QueryBuilder`](/docs/api/url/query#query-builder) writes pairs with the encoding HTML forms use, ready for [`SetQuery`](/docs/api/url/url#set-query).

## Index

### Types

| Name                                                    | Summary                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`UrlError`](/docs/api/url/error#url-error)             | Why text could not be read or resolved as a URL.                             |
| [`QueryPair`](/docs/api/url/query#query-pair)           | One `name=value` pair of a query, both still percent-encoded.                |
| [`QueryPairs`](/docs/api/url/query#query-pairs)         | A walk over a query's pairs, in order, skipping empty ones.                  |
| [`QueryBuilder`](/docs/api/url/query#query-builder)     | Builds a query from `name=value` pairs, encoding each the way HTML forms do. |
| [`HostKind`](/docs/api/url/url#host-kind)               | What a URL's host is.                                                        |
| [`Url`](/docs/api/url/url#url)                          | An absolute URL in normalized form.                                          |
| [`SegmentIterator`](/docs/api/url/url#segment-iterator) | A walk over a path's segments, between its `/`s.                             |

### Functions

| Name                                   | Summary                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Pairs`](/docs/api/url/query#pairs)   | The pairs of `query`, a query without its `?`, such as the one [`Url::Query`](/docs/api/url/url#query) returns. |
| [`Decode`](/docs/api/url/query#decode) | Decodes a percent-encoded component into text.                                                                  |
